title: KCET 2023 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column B2

questions.q: A pair of compounds having the same boiling points are
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: (+)- and (-)-butan-2-ol are enantiomers with identical physical properties, including boiling point, whereas the other pairs are positional isomers or entirely different compounds with different boiling points.

questions.q: Identify A, B and C in the sequence: CH$_3$CH$_2$Br $\xrightarrow[alc]{KCN}$ A $\xrightarrow{LiAlH_4}$ B $\xrightarrow[0^\circ C]{HNO_2}$ C
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KCN gives the alkyl cyanide CH$_3$CH$_2$CN (A); LiAlH$_4$ reduces the nitrile to the primary amine CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$NH$_2$ (B); HNO$_2$ at 0$^\circ$C converts the amine to the alcohol CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$OH (C) via an unstable diazonium salt.

questions.q: CH$_3$-CH=CH-CH$_2$OH $\xrightarrow{PCC}$ CH$_3$-CH=CH-CHO. Hybridisation change involved at C-1 in the above reaction
questions.explanation: PCC oxidises the primary allylic alcohol to an aldehyde without affecting the double bond; C-1 changes from CH$_2$OH (sp$^3$) to CHO (sp$^2$).

questions.q: If a didentate ligand ethane-1,2-diamine is progressively added in the molar ratio en : Ni :: 1:1, 2:1, 3:1 to [Ni(H$_2$O)$_6$]$^{2+}$ aq solution, following co-ordination entities are formed. I. [Ni(H$_2$O)$_4$en]$^{2+}_{(aq)}$ - pale blue. II. [Ni(H$_2$O)$_2$(en)$_2$]$^{2+}_{(aq)}$ - blue/purple. III. [Ni(en)$_3$]$^{2+}_{(aq)}$ - violet. The wavelength in nm of light absorbed in case of I and III are respectively
questions.explanation: en is a stronger-field ligand than H$_2$O, so each successive substitution increases the crystal field splitting $\Delta_o$; the least-substituted complex I therefore absorbs lower-energy, longer-wavelength light (about 600 nm) while the fully en-substituted complex III absorbs higher-energy, shorter-wavelength light (about 535 nm).

questions.q: Which of the following is an organometallic compound?
questions.explanation: An organometallic compound has a direct carbon-metal bond; ethylmagnesium bromide (a Grignard reagent) has a C-Mg bond, while the others are ionic salts with O-metal bonds.

questions.q: A better reagent to oxidize primary alcohols into aldehyde is:
questions.explanation: Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is a mild oxidant that stops the oxidation of a primary alcohol at the aldehyde stage, unlike stronger oxidants such as acidified dichromate, which further oxidise it to the carboxylic acid.

questions.q: In the reaction: C$_6$H$_5$CN $\xrightarrow[(ii)\ H_3O^+]{(i)\ SnCl_2 + HCl}$ X $\xrightarrow{con.\,KOH}$ Y + Z, Formation of X, formation of Y and Z are known by
questions.explanation: SnCl$_2$/HCl followed by hydrolysis reduces the nitrile to benzaldehyde (X) via Stephen's reaction; benzaldehyde, having no alpha-hydrogen, undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated KOH to give benzyl alcohol (Y) and sodium benzoate (Z).

questions.q: Compounds P and R in the following reaction are: CH$_3$CHO $\xrightarrow[(ii)\ H_3O^+]{(i)\ CH_3MgBr}$ P $\xrightarrow[heat]{conc.\,H_2SO_4}$ Q $\xrightarrow[(ii)\ H_2O_2,\,OH^-]{(i)\ B_2H_6}$ R
questions.explanation: P is propan-2-ol (from Grignard addition to acetaldehyde), which dehydrates to propene (Q); hydroboration-oxidation of propene gives propan-1-ol (R). Both have the same molecular formula C$_3$H$_8$O with -OH at different positions, so they are position isomers.

questions.q: Aniline does not undergo
questions.explanation: The Lewis acid catalyst (AlCl$_3$) used in Friedel-Crafts reactions forms a complex with the lone pair on the -NH$_2$ group, deactivating the ring and preventing the reaction; aniline does undergo nitration, sulphonation and bromination.

questions.q: The heating of phenyl methyl ether with HI produces an aromatic compound A which on treatment with con. HNO$_3$ gives B. A and B respectively are,
questions.explanation: HI cleaves the aryl-O bond of anisole to give phenol (A) and CH$_3$I; nitration of phenol with concentrated HNO$_3$ gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol, i.e. picric acid (B).

questions.q: Phenol [ring with -OH] is treated with NaOH to give A; A is treated with (i) CO$_2$ (ii) H$^+$ to give B; B is treated with (i) (CH$_3$CO)$_2$O (ii) H$^+$ to give Y (Major product). Y in the above reaction is
questions.explanation: Phenol + NaOH gives sodium phenoxide (A); the Kolbe-Schmitt reaction with CO$_2$/H$^+$ gives salicylic acid (B); acetylation of the phenolic -OH with acetic anhydride gives aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) as the major product.

questions.q: Sucrose is dextrorotatory but after hydrolysis the mixture show laevorotation, this is because of
options: Laevorotation of glucose is more than dextrorotation of fructose.
Laevorotation of fructose is more than dextrorotation of glucose.
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives an equimolar mixture of dextrorotatory glucose (+52.5$^\circ$) and strongly laevorotatory fructose (-92$^\circ$); since fructose's laevorotation exceeds glucose's dextrorotation, the resulting invert sugar mixture is net laevorotatory.

questions.q: The correct order of match between column X and column Y is: X: I. Vitamin A, II. Vitamin D, III. Vitamin E, IV. Vitamin K. Y: i. Muscular weakness, ii. Increased blood clotting time, iii. Night-blindness, iv. Osteomalacia
options: I - iv, II - iii, III - ii, IV - i
I - ii, II - i, III - iii, IV - iv
I - iii, II - ii, III - iv, IV - i
I - iii, II - iv, III - i, IV - ii
questions.explanation: Vitamin A deficiency causes night-blindness (iii), Vitamin D deficiency causes osteomalacia (iv), Vitamin E deficiency causes muscular weakness (i), and Vitamin K deficiency causes increased blood clotting time (ii).

questions.q: In the reaction: C$_6$H$_5$NH$_2$ $\xrightarrow{P}$ C$_6$H$_5\overset{+}{N}_2$Cl$^-$ $\xrightarrow{Q}$ C$_6$H$_5\overset{+}{N}_2$BF$_4^-$ $\xrightarrow{R}$ C$_6$H$_5$NO$_2$. P, Q and R respectively are :
options: NaNO$_2$ + dil. HCl, HBF$_4$, Cu + NaNO$_2$
NaNO$_2$ + con. HCl, F$_2$, Cu + NaNO$_3$
NaNO$_2$ + dil. HCl, BF$_3$, Cu + NaNO$_2$
NaNO$_3$ + dil. HCl, F$_2$, Cu + NaNO$_3$
questions.explanation: Aniline is diazotised with NaNO$_2$/dil. HCl (P) to give benzenediazonium chloride; treatment with HBF$_4$ (Q) gives the diazonium tetrafluoroborate; Cu/NaNO$_2$ (R) then converts the diazonium group into a nitro group.

questions.q: Thyroxine produced in the thyroid gland is an iodinated derivative of __________.
questions.explanation: Thyroxine is an iodinated derivative of the amino acid tyrosine.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a non-narcotic analgesic ?
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Aspirin is a non-narcotic (non-opioid) analgesic and antipyretic, whereas heroin, codeine and morphine are narcotic (opioid) analgesics.

questions.q: Receptors are proteins and crucial to body communication process. These receptors are embedded in
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Receptor proteins that recognise chemical messengers such as drugs and hormones are embedded in the cell membrane.

questions.q: Which of the following monomers form biodegradable polymers ?
questions.explanation: 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid copolymerise to give PHBV, a biodegradable polyester; the other pairs give non-biodegradable polymers (terylene, nylon/rubber-type materials, and bakelite).

questions.q: Match the List-I with List-II in the following: List-I: 1. Caprolactum, 2. Vinyl chloride, 3. Styrene, 4. Propene. List-II: (a) -(CH$_2$-CH(CH$_3$))$_n$-, (b) -(CH$_2$-CH(C$_6$H$_5$))$_n$-, (c) -(CH$_2$-CHCl)$_n$-, (d) -(CO-(CH$_2$)$_5$-NH)$_n$-
questions.explanation: Caprolactam gives Nylon-6, -(CO(CH$_2$)$_5$NH)$_n$- (d); vinyl chloride gives PVC, -(CH$_2$CHCl)$_n$- (c); styrene gives polystyrene, -(CH$_2$CH(C$_6$H$_5$))$_n$- (b); propene gives polypropylene, -(CH$_2$CH(CH$_3$))$_n$- (a).

questions.q: The correct order of first ionisation enthalpy of given elements is
questions.explanation: First ionisation enthalpy generally increases across period 2, but Be (fully-filled 2s$^2$) and B (2s$^2$2p$^1$) show an anomaly since boron's electron is lost from a higher-energy p-orbital; the correct order is Li < B < Be < C.

questions.q: Which of the following statement is INCORRECT ?
options: Bond length of O$_2$ > Bond length of O$_2^+$
Bond order of O$_2^+$ < Bond order of O$_2^{2-}$
Bond length of O$_2$ < Bond length of O$_2^{2-}$
Bond order of O$_2$ > Bond order of O$_2^{2-}$
questions.explanation: Bond orders are O$_2^+$ = 2.5, O$_2$ = 2 and O$_2^{2-}$ = 1; since 2.5 is greater than 1, the statement that bond order of O$_2^+$ is less than that of O$_2^{2-}$ is false, while the other statements correctly follow from these bond orders.

questions.q: A gas at a pressure of 2 atm is heated from 25 $^\circ$C to 323 $^\circ$C and simultaneously compressed to $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of its original value. Then the final pressure is
questions.explanation: Using $\dfrac{P_1V_1}{T_1}=\dfrac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$ with $T_1=298\,K$, $T_2=596\,K$ and $V_2=\dfrac{2}{3}V_1$: $P_2 = \dfrac{2\times596}{298\times(2/3)} \approx 6\,atm$.

questions.q: Lattice enthalpy for NaCl is + 788 kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $\Delta$H$^\circ_{Hyd}$ = -784 kJ mol$^{-1}$. Enthalpy of solution of NaCl is
questions.explanation: $\Delta H_{solution} = \Delta H_{lattice} + \Delta H_{hydration} = 788 + (-784) = +4\ kJ\,mol^{-1}$.

questions.q: At 500 K, for a reversible reaction A$_{2(g)}$ + B$_{2(g)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2AB$_{(g)}$ in a closed container, K$_C$ = 2 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$. In the presence of catalyst, the equilibrium is attaining 10 times faster. The equilibrium constant K$_C$ in the presence of catalyst at the same temperature is
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up the forward and reverse reactions equally by lowering the activation energy for both, so it does not change the equilibrium constant; K$_C$ remains 2 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$.

questions.q: A weak acid with pK$_a$ 5.9 and weak base with pK$_b$ 5.8 are mixed in equal proportions. pH of the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: For a salt of a weak acid and a weak base, $pH = 7 + \dfrac{1}{2}(pK_a - pK_b) = 7 + \dfrac{1}{2}(5.9-5.8) = 7.05$.

questions.q: Temperature of 25 $^\circ$C in Fahrenheit and Kelvin scale respectively are
The number of protons, neutrons and electrons in the ion $^{32}_{16}$S$^{2-}$ respectively are
questions.explanation: Protons = atomic number = 16; neutrons = 32-16 = 16; electrons = 16 + 2 (for the 2- charge) = 18.

questions.q: A pair of amphoteric oxides is
questions.explanation: BeO and ZnO both react with acids as well as bases, making them amphoteric oxides; Li$_2$O and MgO are basic oxides.

questions.q: The composition of water gas is
questions.explanation: Water gas is a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen, produced by passing steam over red-hot coke: C(s) + H$_2$O(g) $\rightarrow$ CO(g) + H$_2$(g).

questions.q: IUPAC name of the compound H$_3$C(H$_3$C)C=C(CH$_3$)CH$_3$ is
questions.explanation: The compound (CH$_3$)$_2$C=C(CH$_3$)$_2$ is a four-carbon chain (but-2-ene) with methyl substituents at C-2 and C-3, so its IUPAC name is 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene.

questions.q: Among the following: I. Benzene, II. Naphthalene, III. Cyclopentane, IV. Cyclopentadienyl anion, V. Cyclooctatetraene. The set which represents aromatic species is
questions.explanation: Benzene and naphthalene are aromatic (planar, cyclic, fully conjugated, obeying Huckel's 4n+2 rule), and the cyclopentadienyl anion is aromatic with 6 pi-electrons; cyclopentane is not conjugated and cyclooctatetraene is non-planar (tub-shaped) and non-aromatic.

questions.q: Which one of the following gases converts haemoglobin into carboxy haemoglobin ?
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin far more strongly than oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and reducing the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of S in H$_2$S$_2$O$_8$ ?
questions.explanation: H$_2$S$_2$O$_8$ (peroxydisulfuric acid) contains a peroxo (-O-O-) linkage, so two oxygen atoms are effectively at -1 instead of -2; accounting for this, the oxidation number of each S works out to +6, not the naive +7.

questions.q: A 30% solution of hydrogen peroxide is
questions.explanation: Volume strength is roughly (% strength $\times$ 10)/1.7, so a 30% (w/V) H$_2$O$_2$ solution corresponds approximately to '100 volume' hydrogen peroxide.

questions.q: If a stands for the edge length of the cubic systems - The ratio of radii in simple cubic, body centered cubic and face centered cubic unit cells is
questions.explanation: For simple cubic $r=a/2$; for bcc, $4r=\sqrt3\,a \Rightarrow r=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}a$; for fcc, $4r=\sqrt2\,a \Rightarrow r=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt2}a$.

questions.q: Dimerisation of solute molecules in low dielectric constant solvent is due to :
questions.explanation: In non-polar (low dielectric constant) solvents, solutes such as carboxylic acids associate into dimers through intermolecular hydrogen bonding, which shows up as an abnormally high molar mass.

questions.q: The swelling in feet and ankles of an aged person due to sitting continuously for long hours during travel, is reduced by soaking the feet in warm salt water. This is because of :
questions.explanation: The salt solution has a higher solute concentration than the swollen tissue fluid, so water moves out of the swollen cells into the surrounding salt water by osmosis, reducing the swelling.

questions.q: A sample of water is found to contain 5.85% $\left(\dfrac{w}{w}\right)$ of AB (molecular mass 58.5) and 9.50% $\left(\dfrac{w}{w}\right)$ XY$_2$ (molecular mass 95). Assuming 80% ionisation of AB and 60% ionisation of XY$_2$, the freezing point of water sample is [Given : K$_f$ for water 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$, Freezing point of pure water is 273 K and A, B and Y are monovalent ions)
questions.explanation: In 100 g of sample, AB gives 0.1 mol (van't Hoff factor i=1.8) and XY$_2$ gives 0.1 mol (i=2.2) dissolved in 84.65 g water; the total effective molality is about 4.73 m, so $\Delta T_f = K_f\times m_{eff} \approx 8.8\,K$, giving a freezing point of about 273 - 8.8 $\approx$ 264.25 K.

questions.q: Match the column A (type of crystalline solid) with the column B (example for each type) : A: P. Molecular Solid, Q. Ionic Solid, R. Metallic Solid, S. Network Solid; B: i. SiC, ii. Mg, iii. H$_2$O, iv. MgO
questions.explanation: H$_2$O (ice) is a molecular solid (P-iii); MgO is an ionic solid (Q-iv); Mg is a metallic solid (R-ii); SiC is a covalent network solid (S-i).

questions.q: A metal crystallises in a body centered cubic lattice with the metallic radius $\sqrt{3}$ A. The volume of the unit cell in m$^3$ is
questions.explanation: For bcc, $4r=\sqrt3\,a \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{4\sqrt3}{\sqrt3} = 4\,\text{\AA} = 4\times10^{-10}\,m$; volume $=a^3 = 64\times10^{-30}\,m^3 = 6.4\times10^{-29}\,m^3$.

questions.q: The resistance of 0.1 M weak acid HA in a conductivity cell is 2 $\times$ 10$^3$ Ohm. The cell constant of the cell is 0.78 cm$^{-1}$ and $\lambda^\circ_m$ of acid HA is 390 S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$. The pH of the solution is
questions.explanation: $\kappa = \dfrac{\text{cell constant}}{R} = \dfrac{0.78}{2000} = 3.9\times10^{-4}\,S/cm$; $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa\times1000}{0.1} = 3.9\,S\,cm^2mol^{-1}$; $\alpha = \Lambda_m/\lambda^\circ_m = 0.01$; $[H^+]=c\alpha=10^{-3}\,M \Rightarrow pH = 3$.

questions.q: In which one of the following reactions, rate constant has the unit mol L$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$ ?
options: Decomposition of HI on the surface of Gold
questions.explanation: Rate constant units of mol L$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$ correspond to a zero-order reaction; the surface-catalysed decomposition of HI on gold is zero order because the metal surface is saturated, while the other reactions are pseudo-first, three-halves and third order respectively.

questions.q: For a reaction, the value of rate constant at 300 K is 6.0 $\times$ 10$^5$ s$^{-1}$. The value of Arrhenius factor A at infinitely high temperature is :
questions.explanation: As T $\to \infty$, $Ea/RT \to 0$, so $k=Ae^0=A$: the Arrhenius factor A is just the rate constant in the infinite-temperature limit. Since Ea isn't given, options depending on it can't be evaluated, leaving A = 6 $\times$ 10$^5$ s$^{-1}$ as the only determinable answer.

questions.q: The rate constants k$_1$ and k$_2$ for two different reactions are 10$^{16}$ $\times$ e$^{-2000/T}$ and 10$^{15}$ $\times$ e$^{-1000/T}$ respectively. The temperature at which k$_1$ = k$_2$ is :
During the electrolysis of brine, by using inert electrodes,
questions.explanation: Due to overvoltage effects, Cl$^-$ is preferentially discharged over water at the anode giving Cl$_2$ gas, while water is preferentially reduced at the cathode giving H$_2$ gas rather than Na metal.

questions.q: Consider the following 4 electrodes: A : Ag$^+$ (0.0001 M)/Ag$_{(s)}$; B : Ag$^+$ (0.1 M) / Ag$_{(s)}$; C : Ag$^+$ (0.01 M)/Ag$_{(s)}$; D : Ag$^+$ (0.001 M) / Ag$_{(s)}$; E$^\circ_{Ag^+/Ag}$ = +0.80 V. Then reduction potential in volts of the electrodes in the order
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation $E=E^\circ+0.0591\log[Ag^+]$, reduction potential increases with $[Ag^+]$; since B(0.1 M) > C(0.01 M) > D(0.001 M) > A(0.0001 M) in concentration, the reduction potentials follow the same order.

questions.q: When FeCl$_3$ is added to excess of hot water gives a sol 'X'. When FeCl$_3$ is added to NaOH$_{(aq)}$ solution, gives sol 'Y'. X and Y formed in the above processes respectively are
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis of FeCl$_3$ in hot water gives a positively charged Fe$_2$O$_3\cdot$xH$_2$O sol that preferentially adsorbs Fe$^{3+}$ ions, while in NaOH solution the sol particles adsorb OH$^-$ ions and become negatively charged.

questions.q: The reducing agent in the given equations : 4Ag$_{(s)}$ + 8CN$^-_{(aq)}$ + 2H$_2$O$_{(aq)}$ + O$_{2(g)}$ $\longrightarrow$ 4[Ag(CN)$_2$]$^-_{(aq)}$ + 4OH$^-_{(aq)}$, 2[Ag(CN)$_2$]$^-_{(aq)}$ + Zn$_{(s)}$ $\longrightarrow$ [Zn(CN)$_4$]$^{2-}_{(aq)}$ + 2Ag$_{(s)}$
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: In the second (displacement) step, zinc metal is oxidised from 0 to +2 while reducing the silver complex back to metallic silver, making Zn the reducing agent used to recover silver in this cyanide extraction process.

questions.q: For the formation of which compound in Ellingham diagram $\Delta$G$^\circ$ becomes more and more negative with increase in temperature ?
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: In 2C(s) + O$_2$(g) $\rightarrow$ 2CO(g), the number of gas moles increases, so entropy increases; since $\Delta G^\circ=\Delta H^\circ-T\Delta S^\circ$ with positive $\Delta S^\circ$, $\Delta G^\circ$ for CO formation becomes more negative as temperature rises, unlike the oxide-forming reactions shown.

questions.q: Which of the following compound does not give dinitrogen on heating ?
questions.explanation: NH$_4$NO$_3$ decomposes on heating to give N$_2$O (not N$_2$) and water, whereas Ba(N$_3$)$_2$, NH$_4$NO$_2$ and (NH$_4$)$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ all liberate N$_2$ gas on decomposition.

questions.q: Aqueous solution of raw sugar when passed over beds of animal charcoal, it becomes colourless. Pick the correct set of terminologies that can be used for the above example. [Table with columns Adsorbent, Adsorbate, Process]
options: Solution of Sugar | Animal Charcoal | Sorption
Animal Charcoal | Solution of Sugar | Absorption
questions.explanation: Animal charcoal is the solid adsorbent, the colouring impurity is the adsorbate held on its surface, and since this is a surface phenomenon it is called adsorption, not absorption.

questions.q: For Freundlich adsorption isotherm, a graph of log (x/m) Vs. log (P) gives a straight line. The slope of line and its Y-axis intercept respectively are
questions.explanation: The Freundlich isotherm $\dfrac{x}{m}=KP^{1/n}$ in logarithmic form is $\log\dfrac{x}{m} = \log K + \dfrac1n \log P$, so the slope is $1/n$ and the y-intercept is $\log K$.

questions.q: In solid state, PCl$_5$ is a/an
options: Covalent solid present in the form of P$_2$Cl$_{10}$
questions.explanation: In the solid state, PCl$_5$ exists as an ionic compound composed of tetrahedral [PCl$_4$]$^+$ cations and octahedral [PCl$_6$]$^-$ anions.

questions.q: In which one of the following pairs, both the elements does not have (n-1)d$^{10}$ns$^2$ configuration in its elementary state ?
questions.explanation: Zn, Cd, Hg and Cn (Group 12) all have the (n-1)d$^{10}$ns$^2$ configuration, but Cu is [Ar]3d$^{10}$4s$^1$ and lacks this configuration, so the Cu, Zn pair is the one where it is not true that both elements have it.

questions.q: Which of the following is CORRECT with respect to melting point of a transition element ?
questions.explanation: Mn has an anomalously low melting point among the 3d transition metals because its half-filled 3d$^5$4s$^2$ configuration gives weaker metallic bonding, so Cr has a distinctly higher melting point than Mn.

questions.q: aMnO$_4^-$ + bS$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ + H$_2$O $\longrightarrow$ xMnO$_2$ + ySO$_4^{2-}$ + zOH$^-$. a and y respectively are
questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 to +4 (gain of 3e$^-$) and each S in S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ goes from +2 to +6 in SO$_4^{2-}$ (loss of 4e$^-$ per S, 8e$^-$ per S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$); balancing electrons, $3a=8b$ gives a=8, b=3, and since each S$_2$O$_3^{2-}$ gives 2 SO$_4^{2-}$, y=2b=6.

questions.q: Which formula and name combination is INCORRECT ?
questions.explanation: In [CoCl$_2$(en)$_2$]Cl, the two Cl$^-$ ligands inside the coordination sphere plus one Cl$^-$ counter-ion require cobalt to be +3, so the correct name is cobalt(III), not cobalt(II) as given; the other three formula-name pairs are correctly assigned.

questions.q: Which of the following system in an octahedral complex has maximum unpaired electrons ?
questions.explanation: d$^9$(high spin) has 1 unpaired electron, d$^6$(low spin) has 0, d$^4$(low spin) has 2, while d$^7$(high spin) has 3 unpaired electrons (t$_{2g}^5$e$_g^2$), the maximum among these.

questions.q: The correct decreasing order of basicity of hydrides of Group-15 elements is
questions.explanation: Basicity of Group-15 hydrides decreases down the group as the lone pair becomes more diffuse and less available for donation, giving the order NH$_3$ > PH$_3$ > AsH$_3$ > SbH$_3$.

questions.q: Which one of the following oxoacids of phosphorus can reduce AgNO$_3$ to metallic silver ?
questions.explanation: H$_3$PO$_2$ (hypophosphorous acid) has two P-H bonds and is the strongest reducing oxoacid of phosphorus, capable of reducing AgNO$_3$ to metallic silver.
